question: A and B working together can do a piece of work in 4 days. B alone can do the same work in 36 days. How long (in days) will A alone take to do double the work?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(4, 36) = 36 units.

Efficiency of (A+B) = 36 ÷ 4 = 9 units/day.

Efficiency of B = 36 ÷ 36 = 1 unit/day ⇒ Efficiency of A = 9 − 1 = 8 units/day.

Double work = 36 × 2 = 72 units.

Time taken by A = 72 ÷ 8 = 9 days.

**∴ Answer = 9**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A and B together = 4 days

Time taken by B alone = 36 days

**Formula used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time Taken

Time = Total Work ÷ Efficiency

 Work (36 units) Double (36 units) 
• Total Work = 72 units Eff (A+B) = 9 Eff (B) = 1 A's Time = 72 ÷ 8 = 9 Days 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let total work be LCM of 4 and 36 = 36 units.

⇒ Efficiency of (A + B) = 36 ÷ 4 = 9 units/day.

⇒ Efficiency of B = 36 ÷ 36 = 1 unit/day.

⇒ Efficiency of A = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of B

⇒ Efficiency of A = 9 − 1 = 8 units/day.

⇒ Double the work = 36 × 2 = 72 units.

⇒ Time taken by A to do 72 units = 72 ÷ 8 = 9 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 9, which is option (1).**
